Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits — proposed guardband reconciliation language

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the fast demos last week — Brightline is excited about the latency profiles you showed. Procurement ran the Pricing Exhibit you sent by legal and they've flagged the ‘guardband reconciliation’ annex (Section B.3) as ambiguous regarding the interaction between the annual true-up floor and the monthly burst cap.

Specifically: if monthly usage spikes cause us to hit the cap and trigger a temporary surcharge, how does that reconcile against the annual floor true-up? Our counsel is worried the current language could allow a retrospective invoice that double-bills both the monthly surcharge and the annual true-up on the same usage. We attached a redline (Brightline_Redline_v3.docx) with suggested edits — mostly clarifying order of operations and adding a mitigation carveout for a 30-day measurement window.

Can you confirm Redwood’s position on:
- whether monthly surcharges are applied before or after the annual true-up calculation;
- whether there’s a prioritization (i.e., surcharges as temporary credits against future true-ups); and
- whether the proposed 30-day window is operationally feasible on Redwood Dedicated?

Sagar

Sagar — thanks for sending the edits and flags. I forwarded to Legal and Product for ops feasibility (cc'd Marissa and Karthik). Quick answers before legal chimes in: we do not intend to double-bill the same token. Practically speaking:

- Monthly surcharges are applied as a discrete charge for that billing period.
- The annual true-up runs after the contract year closes and reconciles committed vs actual usage; surcharges are treated as separate line-items and are not re-counted into the committed units calculation.
- The 30-day measurement window is reasonable from an infra perspective for Dedicated, but we need to confirm the exact window semantics and how cache/prefix credits are attributed.

I'll let Marissa provide the formal redline language. If we can align on the prioritization semantics we can accept a carveout similar to your suggestion.

Next steps: Marissa, can you review Brightline_Redline_v3.docx and suggest clean contract language that ties the surcharge reconciliation to discrete invoice line-items and excludes those same tokens from annual committed-unit true-ups? Karthik, flag any commercial implications on margin if we adopt the carveout.

Sagar — thanks for the redline and the clear callouts. I pulled Legal + Billing on this thread. Below are proposed contract edits (extracts) and rationale. I attached an annotated version in the doc for line-by-line review.

Proposed extracts (for insertion into Exhibit B — Guardband Reconciliation):
1) "Order of Reconciliation": For avoidance of doubt, any monthly surcharge or temporary overage fee invoiced in a given billing period shall be recorded as a discrete invoice line-item and shall not be counted toward the calculation of annual committed-unit true-up obligations.
2) "Measurement Window Exception": If a usage spike occurs and meets the criteria for a surcharge, Customer may request a 30-day post-spike review window during which Customer may provide supporting logs demonstrating the spike was an anomalous event. If Customer’s logs substantiate an anomaly, Redwood will waive the surcharge for that monthly period or apply an equivalent credit.
3) "No Double Recovery": Redwood expressly disclaims any right to recover both a monthly surcharge and the same usage amount as part of an annual committed-unit true-up; the parties agree credits applied under Section 2 shall be reflected in the annual reconciliation.

Rationale: these snippets ensure commercial predictability and avoid retrospective double-billing. Operationally, Billing will need the spike/logs format (timestamped request ids and aggregate token count) and a 30-day SLA to evaluate.

Open items for discussion:
- whether Brightline needs the review window to be automatic (we propose it be Customer-initiated to avoid workload spikes on Billing)
- how to treat surcharges that were already refunded/credited in the monthly statement prior to annual true-up. Our suggested language would exclude any refunded line-item from annual reconciliation.

I attached the annotated redline: Brightline_Redline_v3_annotated.docx (Word doc, 18KB) and a simple sample CSV schema for logs. Please review and advise. If acceptable, I can prepare a clean Order Form exhibit to swap into the MSA.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marissa — appreciate the quick, concrete language. A few clarifying Qs from our side after reviewing the annotated doc: 

1) On the Measurement Window Exception: would Redwood accept a two-strike cap — i.e., Brightline can request up to two spike reviews per contract year without charge, after which continued reviews incur a $X flat fee?
2) On the No Double Recovery clause: please confirm that refunded monthly surcharges will be excluded from the annual committed-unit calculation even if the refund posts after we run the preliminary annual reconciliation (we often receive late credits in Q1).

If you can confirm both points, Procurement is comfortable moving the redline forward and we can have our legal team sign the amended exhibit. Otherwise we'll need to carve a narrow late-credit exception.

Sagar — quick answers and confirmed language edits below.

1) Two-strike review cap: Redwood accepts the two (2) no-charge spike reviews per contract year proposal; additional review requests will be subject to a nominal administrative fee of $250 per review. Language proposal: "Customer is entitled to two (2) spike review requests per Contract Year without charge; additional review requests will be billed at $250 per request."

2) Late credits/refunds: Redwood will exclude any refunded monthly surcharges from the annual committed-unit true-up calculation provided the refund posts within 60 days of the preliminary reconciliation. Language proposal: "If a refund or credit for a monthly surcharge posts within sixty (60) days of the preliminary annual reconciliation, such refund shall be excluded from the annual committed-unit calculation; refunds posted after such 60-day window shall be handled per the parties' dispute resolution process."

Operational notes for Brightline: Billing will require spike artifacts in CSV form (timestamp, request_id, token_count, model_variant). Karthik will coordinate a short import template and confirm how the spike attribution interacts with Dedicated cache credits.

If that looks good, Mateo can push the clean exhibit into the MSA redline set and we can route for signature (DocuSign link included).
